descriptionAdvanced.de: Ollerton, gelegen im Herzen von Nottinghamshire, ist eine Stadt mit zwei Gesichtern: dem historischen 'Old Ollerton' und dem industriell geprägten 'New Ollerton'. Während das alte Dorf auf eine lange landwirtschaftliche Tradition zurückblickt, wurde die moderne Stadt durch die Eröffnung der Ollerton Colliery im Jahr 1925 geformt. Dieser Bergbaubetrieb zog Tausende von Arbeitern an und prägte das soziale Gefüge bis zu seiner Schließung im Jahr 1994. Ollerton gilt heute als idealer Ausgangspunkt für Erkundungen des Sherwood Forest, der Heimat von Robin Hood. Die Architektur der Stadt spiegelt diesen Wandel wider, von reetgedeckten Häusern im alten Kern bis hin zu den typischen Arbeitersiedlungen des 20. Jahrhunderts.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Ollerton egy történelmi jelentőségű település Nottinghamshire szívében, amelynek története szorosan összefonódik a brit szénbányászattal. A város eredetileg mezőgazdasági közösség volt, de a 20. század elején a bányanyitás radikálisan átformálta az életét, és Ollerton Pit a régió egyik legfontosabb ipari központjává vált. A bánya 1994-es bezárása után a település sikeresen újította meg önmagát, megőrizve ipari örökségét, miközben turisztikai központtá vált a közeli Sherwood-i erdő látogatói számára. A Maun-folyó partján fekvő városközpontban még ma is látható a történelmi vízimalom, amely az egyik legfontosabb épített emlék a környéken. A látogatók számára Ollerton tökéletes kiindulópont a Robin Hood legendáihoz köthető erdőségek felfedezéséhez, miközben a város utcái a régi bányászházakkal és a modern fejlesztésekkel a vidéki Anglia folyamatos átalakulását szemléltetik.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Ollerton este o așezare istorică din Nottinghamshire, a cărei evoluție reflectă transformările industriale ale Angliei rurale. Inițial un sat agricol liniștit, Ollerton s-a dezvoltat spectaculos în secolul al XX-lea odată cu deschiderea minei de cărbune locale, care a devenit centrul vital al comunității timp de decenii. După închiderea minei în 1994, orașul a trecut printr-un proces de regenerare urbană, punând accent pe conservarea patrimoniului său și pe valorificarea locației strategice lângă pădurea Sherwood. Un simbol al trecutului său pre-industrial este moara de apă istorică de pe malul râului Maun, care rămâne o atracție majoră pentru vizitatori. Astăzi, Ollerton servește ca o bază excelentă pentru explorarea legendarei păduri Sherwood și a peisajelor din jur, oferind un amestec interesant de arhitectură victoriană, moștenire minieră și facilități moderne, fiind un exemplu de reziliență a comunităților din nordul Angliei.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Ollerton is a historic settlement in Nottinghamshire that serves as a fascinating example of the shifting tides of English industrial history. Originally a small agricultural village, its character was fundamentally altered in the early 20th century by the opening of the Ollerton Colliery, which turned it into a thriving mining community. Since the pit's closure in 1994, the town has reinvented itself as a residential and tourism hub, leveraging its prime location on the edge of the legendary Sherwood Forest. The older part of the town, known as Ollerton Village, retains much of its traditional charm, centered around a historic watermill on the River Maun that dates back centuries. Visitors often use Ollerton as a gateway to explore the nearby forest trails and the Major Oak, while the town itself offers a glimpse into both the medieval roots and the hard-working industrial heritage of North Nottinghamshire.

en.q: How close is Ollerton to Sherwood Forest?
en.a: It is located on the very edge; the famous Major Oak is only about 3 miles away.

en.q: Can you visit the old coal mine?
en.a: The colliery site has been redeveloped into a business park, but memorials to the miners remain.

en.q: What makes the Ollerton Watermill famous?
en.a: It is the only working watermill in Nottinghamshire and is a popular heritage tea room.

en.q: Are there hotels in Ollerton for tourists?
en.a: Yes, there are several historic coaching inns and modern hotels serving forest visitors.
